effects: Adds a registry-whitelisted adapter to the delegator's ordered adapter list. This list sets the order for deallocation and sweeps.
Grants ALLOCATE_ROLE and DEALLOCATE_ROLE to the adapter address, so the adapter can call allocate and deallocate on the vault's assets.
Nothing of the signer's moves and no native value is taken (not payable).
formats.shown: Add adapter <adapter> on the named delegator.

findings.title: addAdapter also grants the Allocate and Deallocate roles to the adapter, and the screen does not say so.
findings.evidence: UniversalDelegator.sol addAdapter: `_grantRole(ALLOCATE_ROLE, adapter); _grantRole(DEALLOCATE_ROLE, adapter);`. Descriptor intent is "Add allocation adapter" with fields Delegator and Adapter only.
findings.fix: Say it in the intent, e.g. "Add adapter {adapter} and give it allocate/deallocate rights".

effects: Removes the adapter from the ordered adapter list and from the auto-allocate route. Reverts if the adapter still holds assets.
Revokes the adapter's ALLOCATE_ROLE and DEALLOCATE_ROLE.
Sets the adapter's absolute and share limits to zero and clears its pending entry.
formats.shown: Remove adapter <adapter> from the named delegator.

findings.title: removeAdapter also revokes the adapter's roles, zeroes its limits and drops it from the auto-allocate route.
findings.evidence: UniversalDelegator.sol removeAdapter: `_removeOrdered(autoAllocateAdapters, adapter); _revokeRole(ALLOCATE_ROLE, adapter); ... absoluteLimitOf[adapter] = 0; shareLimitOf[adapter] = 0;`. These undo what addAdapter set up, so they are what 'Remove adapter' means.
findings.fix: Optional: "Remove adapter {adapter} and revoke its rights".

effects: Sets the adapter's absolute asset cap to `assets`.
Sets the adapter's share cap to `share`, scaled so that 1e18 = 100% of vault total assets. The effective limit is the smaller of the two caps.
Reverts if the adapter is not added or share > 1e18.
formats.shown: Cap <adapter> at the smaller of <assets> USDC and <share>% of vault assets.

findings.title: setLimits renders the unlimited sentinel as "No absolute cap USDC", with a stray token suffix.
findings.evidence: Case 3 interpolatedIntent: "Cap 0x2222… at the smaller of No absolute cap USDC and 100% of vault assets". The descriptor's threshold message is "No absolute cap" and the wallet adds the ticker.
findings.fix: None at descriptor level; the wallet appends the symbol to threshold messages.

effects: Swaps the positions of two adapters in the `adapters` array. This array sets the order used for deallocation, sweeps and delayed deallocation requests.
It does not change the auto-allocation order, which is `autoAllocateAdapters`.
Reverts if either adapter is not in the list.

findings.title: swapAdapters says "adapter priority" but only changes the deallocation/sweep order, not the allocation order.
findings.evidence: UniversalDelegator.sol swapAdapters swaps entries of `adapters`. _deallocateAll and _sweepPending iterate `adapters`, while _allocateAll iterates `autoAllocateAdapters`. Descriptor intent: "Swap adapter priority".
findings.fix: Intent "Swap deallocation order" and interpolatedIntent "Swap {adapter1} and {adapter2} in the withdrawal order".

effects: Replaces the whole auto-allocation route with the given ordered list of added adapters. Deposits and allocateAll fund the adapters in this order.
An empty list clears the route, which turns off automatic allocation of deposits.
formats.shown: Set allocation order for <delegator>, with each adapter listed in order.

findings.title: setAutoAllocateAdapters with an empty list turns off auto-allocation, but the screen only says "Set allocation order".
findings.evidence: Case 8 ("Clear automatic allocation route") shows only the Delegator field and "Set allocation order for 0xdC94…". The code does `autoAllocateAdapters = newAutoAllocateAdapters;` and onDeposit → _allocateAll iterates this list.
findings.fix: Use "Replace automatic allocation order" so the signer knows the old route is overwritten. Note that an empty list disables auto-allocation.

effects: First runs _sweepPending: deallocates every adapter's free assets back to the vault, deallocates more to cover the withdrawal queue, fills the queue and requests delayed deallocations.
If withdrawals are still pending, returns 0 and allocates nothing.
Otherwise pulls up to `assets` of the vault's free assets into the adapter. The amount is capped by vault free assets, adapter allocatable and the adapter limit.
formats.shown: Request <assets> USDC to <adapter>, labelled Maximum allocation.

findings.title: allocate first sweeps pending withdrawals across all adapters and may allocate nothing; the screen does not say so.
findings.evidence: UniversalDelegator.sol allocate: `if (_sweepPending() > 0) { return 0; }`. _sweepPending calls _deallocate on every adapter and WithdrawalQueue.fill(). The descriptor shows only "Request {assets} to {adapter}".
findings.fix: Intent "Allocate vault assets (after settling pending withdrawals)".

effects: Runs _sweepPending first and returns 0 if withdrawals are still pending.
Deallocates from adapters in list order to free `assets` minus vault free assets. Returns 0 if it cannot free enough, but the deallocations already done stay.
Allocates up to `assets` to the adapter, within its limits.
formats.shown: Allocate, pulling from other adapters: request <assets> USDC to <adapter>.

findings.title: allocateExact has no threshold, so uint256 max shows as a 78-digit USDC amount.
findings.evidence: Case 12 shows "Request 115792089237316195423570985008687907853269984665640564039457584007913129.639935 USDC to 0x1111…". The `#.assets` params have no threshold/message, unlike the sibling formats.
findings.fix: Add `threshold: 0xff…ff` with a message such as "Maximum request (uint256 max)".

findings.title: allocateExact also sweeps pending withdrawals first, and deallocations stay when the allocation returns 0.
findings.fix: Optional wording on settling pending withdrawals first.

effects: Runs _sweepPending first and returns 0 if withdrawals are still pending.
Allocates up to `assets` of vault free assets across the auto-allocate route in order, within each adapter's limits.
formats.shown: Allocate up to <assets> USDC across adapters.

findings.title: allocateAll sweeps pending withdrawals first and may allocate nothing; the route used is stored, not shown.
findings.evidence: UniversalDelegator.sol allocateAll: `if (_sweepPending() > 0) return 0; return _allocateAll(assets);`. _allocateAll iterates the stored autoAllocateAdapters.
findings.fix: Optional: mention that pending withdrawals are settled first.

effects: Deallocates up to `assets` from the named adapter back to the vault.
Then runs _sweepPending: deallocates every adapter's free assets, deallocates more to fill the withdrawal queue, fills it and requests delayed deallocations.
formats.shown: Deallocate request: <assets> USDC, with the adapter in a separate field.

findings.title: deallocate's interpolatedIntent omits the adapter that the assets are pulled from.
findings.evidence: Descriptor interpolatedIntent: "Deallocate request: {assets}". The adapter appears only as a field (case 15).

findings.title: deallocate then sweeps all adapters and fills the withdrawal queue, which the screen does not mention.
findings.fix: Optional: mention that pending withdrawals are processed afterwards.

effects: Deallocates up to `assets` from adapters in list order back to the vault.
Then runs _sweepPending: fills the withdrawal queue and requests delayed deallocations.
Runs _sweepPending first. If withdrawals are still pending, returns 0 and deallocates nothing more.
Otherwise deallocates up to `assets` from adapters in list order back to the vault.
formats.shown: Deallocate after queue fill: request <assets> USDC.

findings.title: deallocateExact's intent "Deallocate after queue fill" does not say it does nothing while withdrawals stay pending.
findings.evidence: UniversalDelegator.sol deallocateExact: `if (_sweepPending() > 0) { return 0; } return _deallocateAll(assets);`. The intent wording is vague for a non-expert.
findings.fix: Intent "Settle pending withdrawals, then deallocate across adapters".

effects: Deallocates up to min(assets, adapter total) from the adapter now.
Requests delayed deallocation of the rest from the adapter.
Lowers the adapter's absolute cap to its remaining assets (never raises it). The share cap is kept.
Then runs _sweepPending.
formats.shown: Deallocate adapter and lower its cap: request deallocation <assets> USDC, with the adapter in a field.

findings.title: forceDeallocate's interpolatedIntent omits the adapter whose cap is lowered and whose assets are pulled.
findings.evidence: Descriptor interpolatedIntent: "Request deallocation: {assets}". The adapter is only a field (case 21). The code calls `_setLimits(adapter, Math.min(absoluteLimitOf[adapter], ...), ...)`.
findings.fix: Use "Force-deallocate {assets} from {adapter} and lower its cap".

findings.title: forceDeallocate's new cap is computed on chain and cannot be shown.
findings.evidence: UniversalDelegator.sol forceDeallocate: `adapterTotalAssets.saturatingSub(deallocated).saturatingSub(pending)` depends on adapter state.

effects: Permissionless. Deallocates every adapter's free assets to the vault, deallocates more to cover queued withdrawals, fills the withdrawal queue, and resets or places delayed deallocation requests on adapters.
Nothing of the signer's moves.
Grants `role` on the delegator to `account`. The caller must hold the role's admin role (DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE).
Allocate/Deallocate holders can move vault assets between the vault and adapters. Default admin can grant and revoke every role.
formats.shown: Grant <role name> to <account>, with the raw role ID also shown.

findings.title: grantRole shows unknown role IDs as a 78-digit decimal in the intent.
findings.fix: None at descriptor level; the enum has no fallback.

effects: Revokes `role` from `account`. Reverts for Allocate/Deallocate on an adapter that is still added.
formats.shown: Revoke <role name> from <account>, with the raw role ID.

effects: The signer gives up `role` on the delegator. callerConfirmation must equal the signer.
formats.shown: Renounce <role name> for <address>, with the raw role ID.

findings.title: renounceRole's sentence does not say the signer loses the role themself.
findings.evidence: Descriptor interpolatedIntent: "Renounce {role.[0:32]} for {callerConfirmation}". OZ renounceRole requires `callerConfirmation == _msgSender()`.

effects: Sets the Ownable owner of the delegator to newOwner. The caller must be the current owner (the vault).
In this contract the owner has no gated functions, and roles and `vault` do not change.

findings.title: transferOwnership moves only the Ownable owner, which gates nothing in UniversalDelegator.
findings.evidence: No `onlyOwner` use exists in UniversalDelegator.sol or MigratableEntity.sol. Roles are under AccessControl, and _initialize sets `vault = owner`.

couldNotCheck: VaultV2, WithdrawalQueue and the adapter contracts called by pull/push/fill/allocate/deallocate have no source in the directory. So I could not confirm that each delegator's vault asset is USDC, the token every tokenAmount field hard-codes.

Six of the seven deployments (0x44c2…, 0xc601…, 0x073d…, 0xead4…, 0xe7b9…, 0x7e74…) have no contract folder. I could not confirm they run the same UniversalDelegator implementation or have USDC vaults.
